transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. Um, I came in because I just can't stop feeling like I'm a danger and... a disappointment. I had this one near-miss at work, and it just feels like it proves I'm not meant to be a nurse. I just keep thinking that everyone would be better off without me.
When you think that everyone would be better off without you, do you want to die or hurt yourself?

I don't have a plan to actually hurt myself or anything like that. It's more just... I keep having these thoughts that it would be easier if I didn't wake up. Or if I could just disappear. That way I wouldn't be around to mess anything up again.
When you have these fears about being dangerous or making mistakes, do you feel driven to repeatedly check, seek reassurance, or perform another ritual to reduce the anxiety?

No, not really. I don't do any rituals or anything like that. I don't feel the need to go back and check things over and over, either. I mostly just... I just get stuck in my head and feel awful about myself. But I don't do anything specific to try and make the anxiety go away.
How long have you been feeling persistently down and hopeless?
Um, it's been going on for about a year and two months now. It really started right after I graduated high school, when I began my college classes and started working full-time at the clinic.
Since this began, has your depressed mood been present most days, nearly every day?

Yeah, pretty much every day. Most days I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling right in my chest, and it just stays with me. Even when I'm at work trying to act normal, or smiling and talking to my patients in Spanish, I really just feel like I'm barely holding myself together.
During this period, have you lost interest in or stopped enjoying activities that you usually like?

Yeah, I have. I used to do a lot of things to clear my head, like jogging, knitting, cooking, or reading after my classes. But now... I just don't. When I get home, I mostly just sit on my bed in my scrubs. I just can't make myself care about any of it anymore.
How has your sleep been since you started feeling this way?

It hasn't been very good. Um, at night I just lie there... I end up replaying patient charts and medication calculations over and over in my head. And when I finally do manage to fall asleep, I usually wake up way before my alarm even goes off. I wake up already feeling exhausted, and just... scared that I missed something important.
How has your energy been during this time?

I haven't really noticed a change in my energy, to be honest. Um... I mean, I'm definitely tired from not sleeping well, but physically, I still have the energy to get through my shifts at the hospital. So I don't think my actual energy levels have dropped or anything.
Since these feelings began, have you had trouble concentrating or making decisions?

Yeah, I really have. It's... it's been getting harder to focus. I have to read the same medication order or lecture slide over and over again because my brain just feels foggy. And making decisions is hard too. Even small choices, like deciding what to chart first, can just freeze me up completely.
Aside from feeling depressed, do you spend most days worrying excessively about several different areas of your life?

No, not really. I mean, I worry about work and making a mistake with a patient, especially since I haven't been sleeping well, but I wouldn't say I worry about everything in my life. It's mostly just the hospital and my classes that stress me out right now.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite since these feelings began?

Yeah, definitely. Um, I just kind of forget to eat until late in the day now. And when I do remember, I usually just have to force down some crackers or have some coffee. I haven't been trying to lose weight or anything, but my work pants have been getting pretty loose lately.
